sources.title: Progress in High-Dimensional Percolation and Random Graphs
sources.author: Markus Heydenreich and Remco van der Hofstad
sources.edition: Springer book; chapter locators below checked against the author manuscript of 17 March 2017
sources.description: A route from the basic model to mean-field mechanisms, lace expansion, the IIC, finite-size scaling, random graphs, and related models.
sources.coverageNote: Selected chapter-level links, not a statement census. Published-edition pagination and theorem numbering must be reconciled with the accessible author manuscript. Exercises, survey material, and open problems remain in scope. Chapter 1 of the dated author manuscript is now read and reconciled in a scoped map. Written spatial/Fourier averaging proofs and the uniqueness-dependent two-point limit are supplied. Remaining inputs and historical predictions are explicit; no published-edition or compiled correspondence is asserted. Section 2.1 is reconciled in the regular-tree map: corrected extinction conditioning, a forest hitting identity, exact root size laws, real-order moment asymptotics and the critical-survival logarithm. Four provisional manuscript errata have written fixes; published-edition comparison and Section 2.2 reconciliation remain pending. Section 2.2 is now mapped: root-corrected occupation, exact coordinate and second-moment lengths, and critical spatial-radius comparison bounds. The fifth provisional manuscript entry repairs generation zero. An exact radius amplitude, Chapter 3 and published-edition comparison remain separate. Chapter 3 now has a reading map and written repairs for finite-set coordinate support, the all-radius rate, boundary multiplicities, field mass and inverse endpoints. Finite-torus approximation now supplies both Aizenman–Barsky inequalities and the pointwise scalar bound; the half-space exercises remain separate work. Further supporting proofs supply nearest-neighbour uniqueness, finite pivotal sets under half-space positivity, the integrated zero-field inequality and exact tail-to-field asymptotics. The half-space premise and full-text Chayes–Chayes comparison remain explicit. Chapters 4 and 5 now have reading maps: global reciprocal control, small-triangle susceptibility, critical nonpercolation, uniform and shifted walk diagrams, and spread-out symbol bounds. Infrared estimates remain explicit premises; their lace proof and bare-triangle regularization stay separate. Two further provisional discrepancies have written fixes, respectively local and statement-level. Chapter 6 now has a cutting-bond and finite-expansion proof, with a positive recursion, explicit remainder norms and conditional full-expansion/critical-limit criteria. Coefficient bounds and the bootstrap remain separate. Chapter 7 now has disjoint-witness proofs, all-order geometric mass bounds, the first weighted estimate and a critical-convergence criterion. The refined and general weighted bounds, signed moments and the infrared bootstrap remain separate tasks. The signed-moment discussion is now reconciled with an absolute-moment convolution identity, the nonnegative Fourier converse and a coefficient criterion for the effective quadratic term. All-order frequency bounds and the bootstrap remain premises. The reversed-chain exercise, all-order weighted coefficient estimate and refined first coefficient now have full written proofs. The conditional frequency summation gives absolute moments; Chapter 8 must still supply the frequency-diagram bounds and bootstrap. Chapter 8 now has reciprocal algebra, the positive walk estimate and continuity of the bootstrap functions. A provisional statement-level sign repair has a complete proof. The quantitative diagram bounds and improvement step remain unfinished. Chapter 8 is now fully read: the frequency diagrams, quantitative nearest-neighbour improvement and critical Fourier density have complete written proofs. Two further provisional entries have local fixes. The illustrative ODE, next-order threshold and spread-out exercises remain separate. Chapter 9 now has full written green-free, magnetization, tail and extrapolation proofs. Three provisional entries have complete repairs; density constants are uniform only after rescaling by 2d. Sharp asymptotic amplitudes remain separate. Chapter 10 is fully read: non-backtracking walk and conditional matrix identities are proved, with three provisional summation/support/algebra repairs. The coefficient construction and numerical bootstrap have not been reproduced. Chapter 11 correlation/Fourier deductions now include the near-critical squared-length identity and Fourier amplitude. Two provisional repairs are complete; the reciprocal-mass correction remains partial pending tilted analytic estimates. Chapter 11 is fully read: intrinsic arm bounds are proved from existing volume results, and the conditional extrinsic lower bound and dimension obstruction have complete proofs. Two further provisional event-inclusion/power repairs are complete; extrinsic regularization remains separate. Exercise 11.6 now has a corrected convolution remainder with explicit cancellation and exponent ranges, checked against Hara’s primary Appendix B. The intended spatial transfer remains valid under its separate inputs. Exercise 11.4 now has a written first-coefficient spatial proof using two long edges and four residual summation patterns; all-order bounds and the spatial bootstrap remain separate. The signed-kernel Gaussian input in Section 11.2 now has a complete written analytic proof and conditional lace amplitude; the model-specific all-order pointwise bound and spatial bootstrap remain separate. Chapter 12 is fully read: both IIC two-point upper-bound routes have written proofs; existing cylinder compactness and critical-tree spine results are reused. Full percolation existence/equality, one-endedness and the lower bound remain separate. A noncylinder-limit passage has a complete local upper-proof repair. Section 13.1 is fully read: exploration, uniform binomial progeny estimates and the existing covariance theorem give a complete written critical component-scale proof. Off-window asymptotics and joint scaling limits remain separate. Section 13.2 is fully read: quotient domination, the lattice critical tail and existing rooted damping give the torus exponential upper tail and all positive largest-component moments; hyperscaling gives its susceptibility upper bound. Matching lower bounds and lower bounds for other ordered components remain separate. Section 13.3 is fully read: finite susceptibility levels, exact complete-graph triangle algebra, optimized exponential tails and a one-sided critical-parameter comparison have written proofs. Two provisional formula repairs preserve the final estimates; finite-triangle lower-window inputs and supercritical conclusions remain separate. Section 13.4 is fully read in extracted text. Hypercube mixing has a scalar-recurrence proof and an explicit finite-triangle criterion is written; the hypercube short-loop sum is proved by Fourier moments; critical-location inputs, lower-window estimates and the giant-component proof remain separate. The cited hypercube growth argument is now reconstructed from the earlier Unlacing survey, with corrected collision multiplicities; the susceptibility threshold and the finite triangle up to it have written proofs. The finite-triangle window article now supplies the root lower tail and largest-component scale throughout a bounded degree-normalized window. Exercise13.6 has a provisional parameter-normalization repair with a four-cycle counterexample. The positive-window susceptibility upper bound and off-window giant-component results remain separate. The Chapter 11 moment-gap deduction now has a written proof in the sufficiently-large-dimension classical regime, with degree scaling, fractional moments and fixed-cutoff cluster density. The numerical dimension threshold, general finite-triangle regularization and tilted/spatial inputs remain separate. The actual exponential mass and boundary divergence are now proved using a finite-box tilt argument; the uniform tilted coefficient estimates remain separate, and the reciprocal erratum stays partial. The tilted coefficient bootstrap and exponential correlation-length law now have full written proofs in sufficiently large dimension. The reciprocal correction is marked fix found in that regime; numerical thresholds and source constants remain separate. The higher-lace-moments article supplies all-order polynomial moments and weighted critical continuity under the spatial two-point and small-triangle hypotheses; the all-order pointwise bound remains separate. LKS9 and NI0W give exact finite-return certificates for the sixth walk norms and an explicit connector test: dimensions >=40, >=64 and >=100 suffice under infrared amplitude and j_c bounds 21/20, 11/10 and 23/20 respectively. The percolation infrared input and other critical hypotheses remain conditional; no numerical percolation threshold is claimed. NOTF/66SP/7GNW quantify the existing nearest-neighbour bootstrap: for d>=10^11 the infrared amplitude is at most 521/500 and 2d p_c at most 1001/1000, with all critical hypotheses for FWHO supplied. This coarse independent bound is not attributed to the source and does not establish the earlier conditional low-dimensional cases; all errata and formal statuses remain unchanged. YT0O/E5ZR/9TAI supply explicit susceptibility, critical field/tail, rescaled density and subcritical cutoff constants for d>=10^11, including the cubic second-moment lower constant 1/3 and lower cutoff chi squared/6. This coarse independent range is not attributed to the sources; arbitrary finite-triangle regularization and limiting amplitudes remain separate. ADWR/I23O/7T8L now complete the general finite-triangle mean-field and moment-cutoff implications through the corrected boundary and entropy arguments, with model-dependent constants and no small-triangle hypothesis. The earlier unresolved regularization refers to the classical endpoint-separation proof, which remains a separate route; no new dimension threshold, limiting profile or formal-status change is claimed. 0HRJ/KIGU/Z78U add intrinsic-ball moment bounds for susceptibility-biased cylinder limits and ratio-controlled distant-point limits. Finite triangle gives exponential upper tails on the radius-squared scale and an almost-sure r squared log log r upper bound; matching lower volume and identification of IIC constructions remain separate. KGPE/RG3Z now complete the matching intrinsic lower-volume bound for susceptibility-biased limits under finite triangle and ratio-controlled distant-point limits; 3FTE/POD2 give the history comparison and linear resistance growth. Volume exponent two and resistance exponent one hold almost surely. The Kozma–Nachmias map records the primary exploration arguments and the separate susceptibility-biased extension; random-walk consequences and identification of IIC constructions remain separate.

sources.title: Basic properties of SLE
sources.author: Steffen Rohde and Oded Schramm
sources.description: Trace geometry and derivative moments for ordinary chordal SLE.
sources.coverageNote: Lemma6.3, its geometric interpretation (6.2) and the start of its proof read in the published PDF text, pp.903–904. The moment threshold for ordinary SLE6 is compared with the conditioned law. GXMS supplies a separate percolation-based bound. No full lemma proof, visual-PDF audit or general SLE coverage is claimed. Continuation: Lemma6.3 and its proof through (6.10) have now been read in full in the published PDF text, pp.903–906, and compared with arXiv:math/0106036v4 section6 HTML. LZCO/K0WT/ILR6 provide a complete alternative moment proof through the radius-clock diffusion, Euler positivity, a ground eigenfunction and the scale function. DC8Q derives a terminal domain-boundary distance exponent. Loewner/SDE foundations and standard special-function identities are explicit tools; trace existence, full-trace identification, dimension and the rest of the paper remain uncovered. No new erratum or compiled association. Further continuation: Lemmas 6.5–6.6 and the proof of Theorem 6.4 were read in the published PDF text, pp.906–908, and compared with arXiv:math/0106036v4 section 6. JCIS/6DV8 prove finite physical lifetime for each fixed point when kappa>4 by a half-disk exit estimate. KQIN proves the boundary co-swallowing beta law with a complete diffusion endpoint argument. 2L0Z derives the trace hitting law under the explicitly retained geometric comparison and trace-existence inputs. Theorem 6.4 is read but not reproduced in full; transience, trace construction and dimension remain separate. No new erratum or compiled association. Covering continuation: (6.2), Theorem 8.1 and Corollary 8.2 were compared with the published PDF and v4 HTML. G0UQ proves the distance identification for a continuous generating trace; VEZ7 makes the radius bounds uniform on compact sets; 1424 derives the expected covering exponent as a full logarithmic limit; YBRV proves the Hausdorff upper bound. Separate inner and outer grids repair the provisional localization issue in the displayed comparison on p.912. Trace construction remains an explicit source input, including the cited kappa8 extension; transience, hull-boundary dimensions and Hausdorff lower bounds remain separate. No compiled association. Boundary/transience continuation: Lemma 7.2 and the simple-curve part of Theorem 7.1 were compared in v4 HTML and the journal PDF, pp.909–911. RD3V proves boundary noncollision and the minimum law; JQ3M gives a bounded-potential distortion estimate for every kappa at most four; YBCC and D67E derive fixed-boundary avoidance and transience under the explicit simple-trace theorem and slit prime-end correspondence. The critical potential is extended to smaller kappa by its drift sign. No new source fault or compiled association; transience above four and trace construction remain separate. Space-filling continuation: the large-parameter proof of Lemma 7.3, Theorem 7.1, Corollary 7.4 and their kappa8 update were compared with the journal PDF, pp.910–911. UELC uses density to identify each interior hull with the past trace; KFWY identifies fixed-point hits; ZS6G proves immediate origin engulfment using strong Markov, deterministic-time zero-area boundaries and the germ law; R2A0 derives transience and finite-time coverage of every compact half-plane set for kappa at least eight. The full all-times inverse-map limit in Theorem 5.1 and the area conclusion of Corollary 5.3 remain explicit inputs, read at pp.899 and 901. The intermediate regime, derivative estimates and those input theorems remain separate. No new erratum or compiled association. Derivative continuation: Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, Corollary 3.5 and Theorem 5.2 were compared in v4 HTML and journal PDF text. HHBC identifies reverse flow at fixed time; O0VQ supplies the global height clock and two-sided derivative comparison; AXSH proves all-real-parameter weighted moments; M7AF gives a direct fixed-time tail bound without the borderline logarithm; OLNV proves fixed-time Holder extension for kappa not equal to four, with admissible exponents tending to one half at zero and one at infinity. A separate provisional erratum repairs the nonmonotone derivative comparison in Lemma 3.3, p.893, by a bounded factor valid for every real moment order. The rest of that lower-bound proof, joint-time continuity, trace generation and the boundary-dimension input remain separate; no compiled association. Reading update, 17 November 2026: Section 3.3 now has a complete written joint radial continuity proof using deterministic time grids, together with a time modulus and the almost-every-time kappa-eight conclusion. Section 4 was read; its deterministic trace-generation criterion remains to be supplied. No new erratum or compiled association. The deterministic trace-generation criterion is now proved by first contact of an avoiding arc, with classical boundary theorems explicitly named. It gives the all-times continuous generating SLE trace and full tip limits for kappa different from eight; simplicity and the zero-area boundary input remain separate. Simultaneous real-boundary avoidance and the simplicity theorem for kappa at most four are now proved using rational restarts and strict capacity growth. This supplies the simple-trace hypotheses of the earlier boundary-distance and transience arguments. The interior-point lifetime classification below eight, Exercise 6.7, simultaneous hull-boundary dimension and zero area below eight, and nonempty hull interior at all positive times between four and eight are now proved. The last statement is weaker than origin engulfment; real-boundary swallowing geometry remains separate. Boundary-swallowing continuation: backward real flows and local Schwarz reflection identify the first boundary hit and supply the geometric input for the beta law. The real-point swallowing assertion, immediate origin engulfment and transience between four and eight are now proved, including simultaneous finite lifetimes and finite-time hull coverage of compact sets. Version 4 Sections 6–7 were checked; no new journal-PDF comparison, source erratum or compiled association. The localized hull-boundary proof now supplies fixed-time covering exponent delta, Hausdorff upper dimension and zero area for every positive kappa, including eight without a trace theorem there; it completes transience and finite-time compact trace coverage above eight. Kappa-eight trace construction and the global Whitney-sum threshold and lower bounds remain separate. Existing errata assessments are unchanged. Lemma 3.3 is now proved in full by a tilted-diffusion fractional-moment argument, including the bounded-factor comparison for every real moment order. The expected localized grid sum has the exact boundary-exponent threshold away from kappa four. The existing derivative-comparison erratum links to this full proof; its found/local classification is unchanged. Global Whitney comparisons and their expected-covering consequence remain separate. The global Whitney-sum threshold of Theorem 8.3 and expected-covering lower limsup of Corollary 8.5 are now proved by a direct grid comparison, Gaussian control of the random horizontal window, and removal of large derivative scales. The covering comparison uses a positive height buffer. Lemma 8.4's restricted preimage-interval statement is bypassed rather than separately reproduced. Existing errata assessments are unchanged; no almost-sure or Hausdorff lower bound is claimed. Remark 3.4 now has an explicit endpoint moment kernel in both flow directions, proved by a bounded-coefficient change of measure and the Gaussian hyperbolic coordinate. A reverse height-crossing moment equivalent includes its exact Gamma constant and inverse square-root logarithm. These are random-height-time statements, not fixed-physical-time estimates; the occupation-time tail mentioned in the remark and the kappa-eight trace construction remain separate. Existing errata assessments and compiled evidence are unchanged.

T723 proves the reflected radial product by collecting its logarithmic drift; EU7X proves the mixed boundary limit and all-boundary powers; MLBQ supplies the compact-stopped radial force law; O8ZR derives the equal-weight kappa6/kappa2 candidates. A center mark is removed consistently with the normalized product limit. The source rare-event formulas remain proposed asymptotics, with discrete identification and terminal control outstanding. The general radial coordinate-change theorem and strip interior-force extension remain separate. No new erratum or compiled association. Coordinate continuation: 9BVE derives the half-plane-to-disk normalization and positive clock; 5KL5 transports mixed force points and the residual old-target weight; K4PV proves the stopped inverse law. Theorem 3 and Remark 4 were checked in v3 and the journal. Remark 4 now has a provisional derivative-convention entry: use the modulus of the complex derivative or explicitly the angular derivative. The earlier explicit clock is correct. JVHZ and V2NR prove disk-to-disk target changes directly, retaining the stated interior-target lifetime without an auxiliary boundary stop. The strip interior-force extension remains separate; no compiled association. Mixed-force continuation: C1GN extends the direct half-plane target calculation to interior marks; P3E9 proves the reflected strip force transformation; 8GVO supplies equal compensating endpoint forces for half-plane and disk destinations. Definition 2, Theorem 3 and Section 4 were compared in v3 and the journal. A provisional missing-admissibility entry records that a half-plane destination needs a finite image of the starting point, a condition already explicit in Section 4. sources.title: Decay of correlations in nearest-neighbor self-avoiding walk, percolation, lattice trees and animals

sources.coverageNote: Appendix B is fully read in extracted text and its convolution consequences have written proofs. Selected introductory theorem statements are identified; the Gaussian lemma and model-specific spatial bootstrap remain unread in full. One provisional intermediate sign error has a complete notation repair. No visual-page or compiled correspondence is claimed. Subsequent reading completes Sections 2.1–2.6: the signed-kernel Gaussian lemma and its quantitative remainder now have written proofs. Model-dependent diagrammatic estimates and Appendix A remain separate. A second provisional entry has a complete local Gaussian-normalization fix. The higher-lace-moments article supplies all-order polynomial moments and weighted critical continuity under the spatial two-point and small-triangle hypotheses; the all-order pointwise bound remains separate. Sections 3.4–3.5 and 4.1.1–4.1.2 were read in extracted text. The integer-moment Fourier bridge and first unconditional spatial bound are written; the two-mark and separated-segment diagram steps remain unfinished. Two-route weights now give fourth moments and weighted critical continuity for the zeroth and first lace coefficients without assuming spatial decay; the uniform all-order two-mark estimate remains separate. An alternative planar-dual Holder argument now supplies the qualitative all-order moment gain in sufficiently large dimension, retaining small connector factors; the sharper source dimension range and pointwise spatial bootstrap remain separate. The planar two-edge deletion bound LS5S and long-edge estimate 8F9A now close the qualitative critical spatial asymptotic in KF2I, with its 2/d remainder, while retaining an unspecified sufficiently-large-dimension threshold. Fractional coordinate weights now have Lp Fourier densities and critical convolution identities in AOKO/65QV/ODMM, with strict moment and power-counting conditions; the source directional estimates and non-even endpoints remain separate. The later integrated-modulus argument 2SC4/ENZ7 supplies the exact non-even input-moment endpoint, including odd integers, while retaining strict dimensional power counting. The real-order planar gain PCOC and range 6N01 now remove the even-moment restriction; QKEC closes the spatial arithmetic for d>30 while retaining the critical Fourier and small-connector hypotheses, whose dimension threshold remains unspecified. The weighted middle integral (4.8) now has a direct Lp proof in U7QM/5PWM, with a dimension-seven core estimate and heat regularization of the full spatial identity; the directional estimate and other marked-diagram decompositions remain separate. MAT0 now supplies the directional bound (4.17) for noninteger s with ceil(s)<=K, by splitting the symmetric-difference integral; it retains that integer-input condition and does not replace the separate exact-moment Lp endpoint. Ordered block-face integration and a three-bridge count now give an independent L9 refinement in 7TNU/5T90/RCF3: the reachable moment range is s<7d/9-4. CP1T closes the spatial arithmetic for d>18, retaining the critical Fourier and ninth-norm connector assumptions; no numerical percolation claim at d=19 follows. SL9H and B0RG further improve the moment argument by bounding marked spatial transition rows: every s<d-6 follows from the critical Fourier gap, second moments and 2T Delta<1 when d>10, without assumed Gaussian two-point decay. The pointwise/Gaussian estimate retains its separate ninth-norm condition; no numerical threshold is verified. The sixth-norm endpoint 634L and the moment range B0RG close the conditional Gaussian argument for d>14 in FWHO, followed by coefficient moments and continuity for s<d-4. The balanced heat cutoff 7QGG improves the fourth-moment remainder exponent to 4/(d+2). Numerical percolation smallness at d=15 remains unverified. LKS9 and NI0W give exact finite-return certificates for the sixth walk norms and an explicit connector test: dimensions >=40, >=64 and >=100 suffice under infrared amplitude and j_c bounds 21/20, 11/10 and 23/20 respectively. The percolation infrared input and other critical hypotheses remain conditional; no numerical percolation threshold is claimed. NOTF/66SP/7GNW quantify the existing nearest-neighbour bootstrap: for d>=10^11 the infrared amplitude is at most 521/500 and 2d p_c at most 1001/1000, with all critical hypotheses for FWHO supplied. This coarse independent bound is not attributed to the source and does not establish the earlier conditional low-dimensional cases; all errata and formal statuses remain unchanged.

sources.author: Christian Borgs, Jennifer T. Chayes, Remco van der Hofstad, Gordon Slade and Joel Spencer

sources.coverageNote: Selected passages read: Section4.1 susceptibility bounds; Section5.1 field statements; Section6,Lemmas6.1–6.2 and their proofs; Section3.6 window deductions. The wiki reconstructs the finite field bounds from its existing cutting-bond proof, and proves root tails and largest-component tightness. The positive-window susceptibility upper bound, off-window results and appendices have not been fully reconciled; no journal-text or compiled check is claimed. Subsequent coverage completes the positive-window susceptibility upper bound: Section 8 and Appendix A.3 have now been read, and the wiki supplies a cluster-conditioning proof of marked-volume transport, two-sided window susceptibility and component moments through order two. Other appendices and the journal comparison remain separate. Section 9 and the necessary rectangle and density arguments in Sections 5.2 and 6 are now read and proved in the supercritical article, including nonuniform boundary covariance and the exact concentration regime. A singleton-cutoff proof error has a provisional local repair. Giant-component lower bounds and geometric sprinkling remain separate. The sharper subcritical estimates in Theorem 1.5 and Sections 1.4 and 4 are now reconstructed, with explicit component lower bounds from Section 7. A provisional statement correction retains a positive threshold denominator; susceptibility asymptotics are unchanged. The logarithmic gap in the component bounds is explicit. Appendix A.2 is now compared with the September 2004 author manuscript. That revision already corrects the early diagonal convention and cubic coefficient. A full finite cutting proof and exact K4 scope counterexample supply the positive-part correction. Two provisional entries distinguish the existing author repair from the remaining generic-lemma qualification; the publisher version is still unexamined. Section 2.1.2 and the heuristic (3.10) have now been revisited. P1F1/XF00/X0R0 give a complete-graph tree-count proof of the matching logarithmic lower bound and every fixed-rank leading size in probability and mean absolute normalized error, under epsilon tending to zero and N epsilon^3 tending to infinity. The general-host gap and critical-window joint law remain separate. EMO3/VGZ9/CJ8R further give a written complete-graph second-order extension: cyclic components are negligible at the extreme scale, tree exceedances converge to Poisson laws, and each fixed-rank centered size has the corresponding Gumbel order-statistic limit. The exact rate I is retained; this is not attributed to the cited benchmark passages or extended to the critical window. These are written complete-graph extensions; no extra separation from the window or new source error is asserted. AUTD/2KT9/U6EN complete the barely supercritical complete-graph benchmark: a uniform parabolic exploration profile, a unique giant of size two epsilon N in probability and mean absolute error, and logarithmic sizes in probability for every fixed rank after it. The selected-complement conditioning is explicit. This does not settle the general-host giant lower bound or logarithmic-scale means for the remaining components.

sources.title: Asymptotics in percolation on high-girth expanders
sources.author: Michael Krivelevich, Eyal Lubetzky and Benny Sudakov
sources.edition: Author manuscript associated with arXiv:1803.11553; cited locators use the 22-page author PDF
sources.description: Sharp giant-component asymptotics for percolation on high-girth regular expanders.
sources.coverageNote: The finite-supercritical-clusters map compares Theorem 1 and Section 2.1 with 9906/NVCH/YTZU. The wiki proves the vertex-density limit with a weaker local-tree condition. Edge and degree laws, the 2-core and exponential concentration remain outside this reading; no full-paper coverage or compiled correspondence is asserted. YCHK/UPQ2/OH6B/VSGH now supply exponential fixed-parameter deviations, the giant empirical local law, degree frequencies and edge/excess densities under local tree convergence. The fixed-d excess density has a cubic near-threshold expansion after taking the graph-size limit. The 2-core remains separate. One provisional explanatory-prose erratum has a complete notational repair; displayed formulas and conclusions are unchanged. 0ATK/S8OP/TGLZ/2K74 now give the full fixed-parameter 2-core reconstruction: thick-set red expansion, reserved blue cycle witnesses, edge/local approximation and degree/vertex laws, negligible other cores and negligible giant-core bridges. A second provisional entry has a local repair for the reduced red first-round parameter in an intermediate expectation. Critical-window uniformity remains outside this work. The fixed-parameter expander chapter now also proves uniform resilience under small vertex deletions, absence of small balanced separators, a DFS path separator and linear cycles in the giant and its 2-core. It corrects the direction of the conditional erasure bound in the Theorem 4.1 prose, provisionally/fix found/notation; the next source display already has the correct direction. The complete-minor theorem and near-critical uniformity remain separate.

sources.title: Asymptotic normality of the size of the giant component via a random walk
sources.author: Béla Bollobás and Oliver Riordan
sources.edition: arXiv:1010.4595, 11-page version; journal publication JCT B 102(1), 53–61
sources.description: An exploration-martingale proof of Gaussian fluctuations of the supercritical complete-graph giant.
sources.coverageNote: Theorem 1, Corollary 2 and the full Section 2 proof are read in extracted PDF text. UEXT/WEV8/UKVG/MEUA give a complete written vanishing-epsilon proof and the transition for replacing the survival-probability center by 2 epsilon N. Bounded parameters away from one, joint core fluctuations and centered-moment convergence are outside this reconstruction. No publisher-version comparison, new erratum or compiled correspondence is claimed. The checked arXiv index identifies the 11-page manuscript as v2, revised 16 April 2011. DD9N/OH30/K1HI/KU4Y now combine the written Gaussian marginal with uniform conditioned-complement extreme limits and prove their asymptotic independence. The smaller ordered extremes use exact supercritical rate epsilon-log(1+epsilon). No centered-moment or critical-window claim is added. Y85E/LXGK now prove exponential early-exploration bounds and all centered Gaussian moments, including Var(L1) asymptotic to 2N/epsilon. These are written uniform-integrability arguments extending the marginal distributional law.

sources.title: Component sizes of the random graph outside the scaling window
sources.author: Asaf Nachmias and Yuval Peres
sources.description: Exploration proofs of barely subcritical and barely supercritical complete-graph component-size laws.
sources.coverageNote: Theorem 1.2 and Section 4 are read in extracted publisher-PDF text. The finite-supercritical-clusters map relates the earlier probability proof to the source. N9DF/PMEN/PW6A/DNIW add explicit exponential exploration bounds and all fixed positive leading-scale moment convergence. These moment conclusions are written deductions, not claims made by the cited probability theorem. Centered supercritical moments and a centered law for the remaining ranks remain separate; no new erratum or compiled correspondence is asserted. 7W39 adds joint subcritical interval counts and the ordered extreme vector from exact enumeration. DD9N/OH30/K1HI/KU4Y give centered non-giant extremes jointly with the Gaussian giant, with exact dual normalization, asymptotic independence and the quadratic-rate bias. These are written extensions of the source probability results; centered supercritical moments and joint critical-window limits remain separate. NVPH/M7A4 now give joint centered polynomial moments, the fixed-rank expectation correction and explicit extreme-rank covariances via the conditioned complement. The exceptional event is controlled at the giant scale. Joint critical-window laws and full-range exponential transforms remain separate.

sources.title: Brownian excursions, critical random graphs and the multiplicative coalescent
sources.author: David Aldous
sources.description: Brownian exploration, component excursions and surplus edges in the Erdős–Rényi critical window.
sources.coverageNote: The finite-triangle-window map records Theorem 3 and Sections 2.1–2.2. Written discrete-time exploration and surplus-mark proofs are supplied; ranked excursions and the coalescent remain separate. Section 2.3 is now fully read. 2N9T/59NH/CH8I/M7BY complete the fixed-parameter ranked size/surplus law in l2, with a direct late squared-mass bound. Lemma 25 was read for comparison; parameter evolution and nonuniform models remain separate. Proposition 5, Section 4.2 and Corollary 24 are now read. 3G0K/5HM7/7HLE/Z8T1 give the square-summable construction, attachment control, joint continuity and finite-dimensional critical-parameter law. The possible omitted term in the searchable Lemma 23 text still needs printed-formula verification; no erratum is asserted. Path-space convergence and joint surplus evolution remain separate. O3IS/R8LD/GRSC/TIGK now supply a written J1 path-space extension, using stopped squared-mass control and explicit compact containment. This extension is not attributed to Corollary 24; joint surplus evolution, common-Brownian coupling and expectation limits remain separate. A40L/YN7V/1DEZ/KCRC now give a written moment upgrade: complete-graph susceptibility, all squared-mass moments, polynomially bounded expectations and integrated path moments. These are deductions from existing wiki results; no newly checked source formula or surplus-process theorem is claimed.
